label: Aquinas, I q.12 a.4 co.: Natural knowledge follows the knower’s mode of being
interpretation: A knower’s nature governs what it can know by its natural power. The first reply allows an angel to know God naturally through a likeness present in the angel. The third reply allows a created intellect to be elevated by grace to see the divine essence.
attribution: The passage states that if a thing’s mode of being exceeds the knower’s own, knowledge of the thing according to that mode exceeds the knower’s natural power, which is the premise.
